contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-naver-pay-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/naver-pay/accept-a-payment`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/naver-pay/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-14 identify South Korean Naver Pay acceptance and link to Checkout and Direct API. The May 8, 2026 detail scopes Checkout to South Korean customers and 28 merchant locations including Singapore, KRW line items, a 100 KRW minimum and a 2,000,000 KRW stored-value top-up limit distinct from card passthrough. It lists Checkout payment, setup and subscription modes; the shown Sessions are payment mode (old raw lines 18-103). In Direct API, the merchant server creates a KRW PaymentIntent for `naver_pay`, with `card` the funding default and `points` available. The merchant includes the required NICEPAY disclosure text and terms link on its own checkout page (old raw lines 229-234). Stripe.js confirms with the client secret and `return_url` and initiates the local processor redirect, where the buyer selects an issuer and authorizes (old raw lines 235-255). The return provides `payment_intent` and `payment_intent_client_secret` for status verification. In test mode `requires_action` becomes `succeeded` on authorization or `requires_payment_method` on failure. The dated guide uses `payment_intent.succeeded` for post-payment actions (old raw lines 282-297). source-stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment.md retains the main routes and funding choices but needs email, mode and payment-state qualifications.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/naver-pay/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-14 replace full detail with two variant links. Old raw lines 8-10 and 109-111 show matching routes, so these captures establish navigation change only. Keep the May 8, 2026 KRW and location terms, Checkout mode matrix and URL examples, and Direct API client/server and NICEPAY disclosure scope dated (old raw lines 24-103 and 134-160, 229-282). In source-stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment.md and the reciprocal Korea concept, Naver sample requests omit email; they do not establish a general no-email rule. The May Kakao guide expressly requires email in Direct API (raw/stripe-kakao-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:134-143). The separate May Naver future-payments guide’s `ngn` saving snippets conflict with this guide’s `krw` payment examples, and its automatic capture requirement is scoped to recurring payments (raw/stripe-naver-pay-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:463-528). Keep authorization, browser return, verified payment status and settlement distinct; May tests and event guidance describe payment states and the sample contains a separate `result.error` reference after destructuring `error` (old raw lines 257-309). Keep the May manual `payment_method_types` examples dated and warn reciprocally that the `2026-09-30.endive` Checkout Session and PaymentIntent create endpoints reject this request field with HTTP 400. The Intent error code is `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported`. Dynamic methods or `allowed_payment_method_types` filter for compatibility and `payment_method_types` is the computed response field. The Endive links and REST table control despite the Intent Impact paragraph's different preview label. This version rule gives no account-specific Naver Pay eligibility (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions-2026-11-07.md:5-23; raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:5-36). The May server creation example documents `card` as default and `points` as an alternative, while browser confirmation sends only the type (old raw lines 134-156 and 254-273). On `2025-03-31.basil`, Naver Pay parameters can be set only at PaymentMethod creation; `PaymentMethod#update` cannot modify them on an existing instrument (raw/stripe-changelog-basil-2025-03-31-naver-pay-payment-method-2026-11-07.md:5-25). Whether the server setting carries through the shown browser call remains unverified, and funding selection is a separate concern from payment-method saving.
